headline: Record revenue swamped by a surge in fuel costs
summary_short: Revenue hit a record $16.3B, up 19.3% y/y, but fuel expense rose 67.5% and the company posted a GAAP net loss of $269M (-$0.41 per share).
summary_long: Revenue growth was broad: premium revenue rose 22.9% and Main Cabin 19.5%. Fuel cost $3.85 per gallon, adding $1.9B of expense y/y, which pushed operating income down to $115M from $151M. Unit cost ex-fuel rose 3.0%. Liquidity ended at $11.8B. For Q4 the company guides revenue growth of 19.5%-22.5% and an adjusted loss per share of $0.50-$1.10, assuming fuel near $4.70 per gallon.
confidence_notes: Adjusted EPS (-$0.28) excludes $87M of net special items after tax and is non-GAAP; it is not comparable to the GAAP -$0.17 prior-year figure. Shard eps_usd carries the adjusted value from Yahoo, so no y/y delta is shown for it.

drivers.explanation: The company paid an average of $3.85 per gallon in the quarter, which raised fuel expense by $1.9 billion year over year.
Strength across all geographies and cabins: premium revenue up 22.9%, Main Cabin up 19.5%, and managed corporate revenue up 27.6%.
Total operating expenses grew 19.8%, slightly faster than revenue at 19.3%, with the fuel increase the largest single item.
Management says historically high fuel prices significantly hurt results while revenue set records; focus is on restoring profitability.
